title: Friday Sermon 63: Adam and Eve, Power and Immortality, and the Qiblah (1982-12-03)
source_file: data/sources/playlists/audio-transcripts/63 - Friday Sermon 03 Dec. 1982 By Dr Rashad Khalifa.csv
document_summary: Dean Mahmoud opens with a comparative reading of the two trees in Genesis and the Quranic tree of eternity, examining knowledge of good and evil, immortality, everlasting kingship, Arabic roots, the creation of human bodies from earth, mortality, delegated power, and Satan's promise of absolute power and immortality. He argues that abuses of earthly power repeat Adam's temptation. After prayer, Rashad and Dean discuss Abraham's prayer for a messenger and begin Quran 2:142–145. The change from Jerusalem to Mecca is treated as a test of submission, the Kaaba as the earlier Abrahamic sanctuary, and the community debates the correct qiblah from Tucson, including flat maps, globe geometry, shortest paths, the direction of local mosques, and a dream offered as confirmation.

sections.title: The two trees, knowledge of good and evil, the tree of life, immortality, kingship, and Arabic
sections.summary: Dean Mahmoud compares the Jewish and Quranic narratives of Adam and Eve. Genesis' tree of knowledge and tree of life are set beside Quran 20:120's tree of eternity and everlasting kingship. Arabic roots for kingdom, angel, and eternity are discussed, along with the claim that Arabic is especially capable of carrying revelation.

sections.title: Creation from earth, mortality, Satan's promise of absolute power, and the abuse of delegated power
sections.summary: Dean reads passages concerning creation from clay or soil, the human spirit and senses, death, and return to Earth. He argues that Satan promised Adam and Eve both immortality and absolute power. Every abuse of human authority, violence, or delegated power is described as a repetition of Adam's temptation.

What did the creation verses say about human mortality?

sections.title: Quran 2:129 and 2:151, Abrahamic priority, Tucson's qiblah, globe geometry, and a confirming dream
sections.summary: Dean identifies Quran 2:151 as the verbal answer to Abraham and Ishmael's prayer in 2:129. He argues that the Kaaba predates Jerusalem's temple and represents the original Abrahamic qiblah. Rashad then debates the direction from Tucson, rejects the northeastern great-circle route, favors a slightly south-of-east line, invokes a geography-department answer, and recounts a dream in which the Tucson group faced the Kaaba while others faced incorrectly.
